purpose: Bridge the registered Phase 6 CPI window into the Phase 4 shadow-schedule schema through an explicit one-to-one provider-component binding, without issuing an executable handoff from synthetic or unlicensed evidence.
hypothesis: A deterministic compiler can validate two logical CPI components, produce one non-executable shadow-schedule preview, reject binding and activation bypasses, and emit zero execution permits while credential and rights inputs are absent.

decision_rule.READY_FOR_LICENSED_HANDOFF_PENDING_VENDO: The binding compiler, Phase 4 schedule bridge, failure injections and replay verifier pass, while synthetic inputs produce no executable handoff.
decision_rule.FAIL_ACTIVATION_HANDOFF: A component, schedule, capture, rights, provenance, activation, preregistration or test gate fails unexpectedly.
decision_rule.EXECUTABLE_HANDOFF: Reserved for a future run with a fresh official roster, live credential, approved rights and a licensed immutable pre-release capture.

economic_decision: A handoff is capture-control metadata only. It does not establish an edge or authorize a market-price join, model fit or trade.
out_of_scope: claiming synthetic provider IDs as empirical
issuing an executable handoff from a structural preview
historical reconstruction of a missed window
